title: Edmund and the Autopsy
premise: True-crime podcaster Oscar Yarrow has spent three years documenting the unsolved disappearance of Edmund Voss, a town coroner who vanished the night of a suspicious autopsy. When a confession letter arrives postmarked the day after Edmund's funeral, Oscar realizes the 'dead' witness at the center of her investigation may be alive—and that someone in Hollow Creek has been feeding her curated lies to keep her close. Following the letter's clues, she uncovers that Edmund faked his death to protect the one person he loved: the woman whose murder he was pressured to cover up, and whose sister Oscar unknowingly became. In the end, Oscar must choose between exposing the truth that will destroy the town and honoring the memory of the man who sacrificed everything to keep her safe.
about_author: Lena Almeida is a former forensic archivist from coastal Maine who spent a decade cataloguing cold-case evidence before turning to fiction. Her novels are known for their meticulous procedural detail and their obsession with the quiet moral compromises small towns make.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Oscar Yarrow records the final episode of her podcast's third season on the Voss disappearance, revealing her obsessive filing system and her rule against getting personally involved. A listener letter arrives—but it's postmarked the day after Edmund Voss's funeral, three weeks ago. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional detachment.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: The unsigned letter claims Edmund's autopsy was falsified and names a witness everyone swears died in 1998: Marisol Vane. Oscar cross-references funeral home records and finds the burial was closed-casket, arranged by the town council. Her producer warns her to drop it. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the thrill of a crack in a sealed case.

chapters.title: What the Coroner Kept
chapters.summary: Oscar breaks into Voss's preserved office and finds his private case notes missing a single page—torn out with surgical care. The town doctor, Ruth Calloway, catches her there but instead of reporting her, asks one strange question: 'Did the letter mention water?' POV: Oscar, brief flashback to Ruth. Emotional beat: first hint that allies have secrets.

chapters.title: Marisol, Everyone Says
chapters.summary: Oscar interviews townsfolk about Marisol Vane; every account is identical, rehearsed, wrong. An elderly ferryman lets slip that Marisol left town pregnant the same year Edmund arrived. Oscar realizes the town's story was coordinated. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: isolation—the case is a wall built by everyone she knows.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Following the letter's reference to 'water,' Oscar finds an unregistered grave on the drowned farmland behind the reservoir: Marisol Vane's real resting place, dated two years before her official death. Someone has left fresh flowers. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger, dread of being watched.

chapters.title: Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Oscar confronts Ruth Calloway, who admits she signed the false autopsy under threat but insists Edmund wasn't corrupt—he was protecting someone. Before she can say who, Ruth's office burns down overnight. POV: alternating Oscar and Ruth. Emotional beat: guilt and urgency; the protector has become a target.

chapters.title: Three Years of Listening
chapters.summary: Oscar audits her own podcast archive and discovers her anonymous source—'E.V.'—fed her details only Edmund could know, steering her investigation for three years. He was alive the whole time, teaching her the truth in pieces. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: The Man at the Reservoir
chapters.summary: Oscar stakes out the reservoir and finally meets Edmund Vane—alive, aged, living as the groundskeeper. He confesses: Marisol was his wife, murdered to silence her knowledge of a council crime, and Oscar is her daughter, given away as an infant. POV: Edmund, then Oscar. Emotional beat: the ground gives way—identity rewritten.

chapters.title: Duty of Care
chapters.summary: The council, led by the funeral director, moves to silence Edmund permanently; Oscar is lured to the reservoir as bait. Edmund surrenders himself to save her, forcing the town's complicity into the open as state police arrive mid-standoff. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: love against duty—she refuses to trade him for the story.

chapters.title: Edmund and the Autopsy
chapters.summary: Months later, the trial dismantles the council; Edmund, dying of illness, spends his last weeks teaching Oscar her mother's history. She airs a final episode—not an exposé, but a eulogy—then files away her alphabet of the dead and begins a new notebook with a living name in it. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into inheritance.
